question: Should object-shaped `channelData` be accepted as standalone send content after the shared opaque-payload sanitizer, including internal-source delivery with no visible text?
rationale: This is an intentional expansion of what the outbound runner considers deliverable content; tests can verify mechanics but cannot select the repository’s long-term trust and channel-payload policy.

options.title: Approve the payload-only contract
options.body: Accept safe object-shaped `channelData` as valid standalone outbound content after the existing protected-context sanitization, then require refreshed exact-head proof.

options.title: Require visible or typed content
options.body: Keep `channelData` metadata-only unless visible text, media, presentation, or an explicit typed channel capability is also present.

options.title: Narrow to internal source replies
options.body: Allow channel-data-only delivery only for the internal-source sink and retain the existing content requirement for external sends.

recommendation.title: Approve the payload-only contract
recommendation.body: Accept safe object-shaped `channelData` as valid standalone outbound content after the existing protected-context sanitization, then require refreshed exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing candidate for a cross-cutting agents/outbound policy decision.
